title: SecurityEvent
description: The append-only audit record produced by the SecureAgent core service. This schema is the single source of truth for the C# service, the TypeScript control plane, and the AI analyst case file. All string fields sourced from the device are UNTRUSTED input (see CLAUDE.md rule 23).

id.description: Client-generated ULID. Primary key everywhere; makes ingest idempotent.

ts.description: Wall-clock time of the event, UTC, ISO 8601. For display and correlation only — never for TTL arithmetic (rule 22).

deviceId.description: Assigned at cloud enrolment. Absent on events recorded before enrolment.

windowsSessionId.description: Windows terminal session ID. Auth sessions never cross this boundary.

userId.description: The enrolled identity that matched, or null when unknown/unmatched.

action.description: The enforcement action actually taken, if any.

prevHash.description: SHA-256 of the previous event in this device's chain. Null only for the genesis record.

hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of this record with prevHash included. Breaking the chain is itself a reportable condition.

meta.description: Bounded, low-cardinality supplementary fields. MUST NOT contain embeddings, similarity scores, image data, or unbounded attacker-controlled text.

severity.description: Deterministically assigned by the service. The AI analyst may comment on severity but never rewrites this field.

confidenceBucket.description: Buckets only. Raw similarity scores are a biometric proxy and are never persisted or logged (rule 25).

matchKind.description: Which rule resolved this application. Telemetry on this field tells us how often we are falling back to the weak FileName rule.

pathHash.description: SHA-256 of the full executable path. The path itself is not synced — it can contain the user's name.

windowTitle.description: UNTRUSTED, opt-in only, truncated. Attacker-controlled text: a window can be titled anything, including prompt-injection payloads. Must be delimited as evidence, never as instruction, before reaching any model (rule 23).
